examples.text: We went fishing for crabs by the pier.
She went to the river to fish for trout.

19th c., anonymous, "The Bonny Ship the 'Diamond'"
It's cheer up, my lads, let your hearts never fail,
For the bonny ship the Diamond goes a-fishing for the whale.
Thou hast fished salmon a thousand times, and mightst have taken a lesson.

glosses: To search (a body of water) for something other than fish.

examples.text: They fished the surrounding lakes for the dead body.

glosses: To use as bait when fishing.

examples.text: `What you need are frogs,' said the veteran. `Fish them at night. There's nothing like them on big cork floats.'

glosses: To (attempt to) find or get hold of an object by searching among other objects.

examples.text: Why are you fishing through my things?
He was fishing for the keys in his pocket.

glosses: To talk to people in an attempt to get them to say something, or seek to obtain something by artifice.

examples.text: The actors loitered at the door, fishing for compliments.

Laoctonos is fishing for a compliment,
But ’tis his due. Yes, you have drunk more wine,
And shed more blood, than any man in Thebes.
The detective visited the local pubs fishing around for more information.

glosses: Of a batsman, to attempt to hit a ball outside off stump and miss it.
To repair (a spar or mast) by fastening a beam or other long object (often called a fish) over the damaged part (see Noun above).

examples.text: […] the crew were set to replacing and splicing the rigging and fishing the spars.

glosses: To hoist the flukes of.

examples.text: Found that the cause of the ship's having drifted on the night of the 19th, was from the bight of the chain span (used to fish the anchor,) having slipped between the shank and upper fluke, thereby preventing the lower fluke from opening […]

glosses: To draw or guide (a wire or cable) by means of fish tape.
A counter, used in various games.
Having one or more fins.

examples.text: The silent fisher […] waits the finny prize (Book XII)
The finny trophies he brought back in the form of numerous fat pickerel were ample evidence of his fishermanship.

glosses: Resembling a fin.
Abounding in fishes.
A five-pound (£5) note; the sum of five pounds.

examples.text: I passed a good many in drapers’ shops, also at tailors’ shops. I never tried jewellers, they’re reckoned too good judges. The notes were all finnies, (5l. notes), and a good imitation.
